For example, one student may read a page five times but remember very little. Another student may close the book, explain the key ideas in her own words, and then check what she missed. The second method often helps her remember information better. Short breaks are also useful. Students can walk, drink water, or stretch before returning to their books. Sleep matters as well: studying all night may seem productive, but a tired brain finds it harder to concentrate the next day. A good study plan should include active recall, regular review, exercise, and enough sleep.
